SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. REGIS...
S. 1, Special Br. XXXXXX
REPORT
Date Dec. 20th, 19 39.

Subject: Arthur Gottlieb - communication from H.B.M. Consulate General
dated December 1, 1939.

Made by D. S. Fitts Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

Comm... P...
Si...
C. Crawford

In regard to the advertisement that appeared in
the North-China Daily News dated November 23, 1939
calling for young ladies above sixteen years of age
to be engaged for a dancing ensemble, lengthy en-
quiries have revealed that Arthur Gottlieb, the
Hungarian ex-manager of the now defunct "Pelican"
Night Club, had the intention of organizing a
troupe of dancers to tour Hongkong, Manila,
Netherlands East Indies, Malaya and India. The
response to his advertisement has been very poor
and numerous obstacles have cropped up since he
inserted the notice, he having found that at the
present time in the shape of securing visas for travel
to the locales mentioned.

Gottlieb is quite an experienced man in the
training of dancing troupes and he thoroughly knows
his business in the organization of such ensembles,
and although in an interview he stated that he had
inserted the advertisement on behalf of a Hungarian
named Relotai, now employed with the Cathay Hotels,
there is little doubt that it was his intention to
conduct the troupe for his own benefit. At any rate
he has temporarily dropped the entire idea and is
shortly returning to Tsingtao to arrange suitable
accommodation for his mother, who is due to arrive in this
city from Europe in the near future.

CONFIDENTIAL
To HBM C G
Further to my note
7 Dec 2

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / 20 DEC. 1939 / COMM... NEWS OFFICE）

报告
日期：1939年12月20日。

主题：亚瑟·戈特利布（Arthur Gottlieb）——英国驻华总领事馆1939年12月1日来函。

制作人：D. S. Fitts 转呈人：D. I. Crawford。

Comm... P...
Si...
C. Crawford

关于1939年11月23日《字林西报》（North-China Daily News）上刊登的一则招聘广告，该广告招募十六岁以上年轻女士加入舞蹈团，经 lengthy enquiries（冗长查询/深入调查）显示，现已停业的“鹈鹕”（Pelican）夜总会的前匈牙利籍经理亚瑟·戈特利布，曾有意组织一个舞蹈团，前往香港、马尼拉、荷属东印度、马来亚和印度巡回演出。他对广告的响应非常冷淡，自刊登通知以来出现了许多障碍，因为他发现目前难以获得前往上述地点的旅行签证。

戈特利布在训练舞蹈团方面相当有经验，并且对组织此类乐团的事务非常精通。尽管他在一次面谈中声称，他是代表一位名叫 Relotai（音译）的匈牙利人刊登该广告的，此人目前受雇于华懋饭店（Cathay Hotels），但毫无疑问，他的本意是为了自己的利益来经营这个舞蹈团。无论如何，他已暂时放弃了整个计划，并即将返回青岛，为其母亲安排合适的住所，其母预计不久将从欧洲抵达本市。

机密
致 英国驻华总领事
继我12月7日的便函之后

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / 1939年12月20日 / 通讯新闻办公室）

Gottlieb is a refugee who has been in Shanghai
for some twelve months. He is quite a clever man and
investigation shows that he is in possession of a
fair amount of cash. He cannot be termed an honest
individual as a perusal of the attached file on his
conduct at the "Pelican" Night Club will show, but
despite his failings in this connection, the Cathay
Hotel management still speak very highly of his
business acumen and regard him more as a fool than
a knave.

Nothing is known to this office of his activi-
ties in Europe and though he has seen fit to declare
to me his innocence of the matter in which he was
involved at the "Pelican" he has persistently refused
to make any type of statement to the Police. He
realizes full well that all his movements are now
regarded by this office with a certain amount of
suspicion and should anything be learned in the
future that in any way reflects on his character,
a subsequent report will be immediately submitted.

Ja Giles
D. S.

D. C. (Special Branch)

戈特利布是一名难民，已在上海居住约十二个月。他是个相当聪明的人，调查显示他拥有相当数量的现金。不能称他为诚实的人，因为查阅附件中关于他在“鹈鹕”夜总会行为的档案即可得知，但尽管他在这方面有缺陷，华懋饭店管理层仍然对他的商业头脑评价很高，认为他与其说是个恶棍，不如说是个傻瓜。

本局对他曾在欧洲的活动一无所知，虽然他认为有必要向我声明他在“鹈鹕”卷入的事件中是无辜的，但他一直拒绝向警方作出任何类型的陈述。他完全清楚，本局现在对他的所有行动都持有一定的怀疑态度，如果将来了解到任何有损其品格的情况，将立即提交后续报告。

Ja Giles
D. S.

D. C. (特别处)

Sir Herbert Phillips, K.C.M.G., O.B.E.,
H.B.M. Consul-General,
H.B.M. Consulate General,
SHANGHAI.

CONFIDENTIAL

Dear Sir Herbert:

In reply to your note of December 1,
1939, in regard to an advertisement in the "North-
China Daily News", this is already under investi-
gation by the Special Branch. The advertiser,
Gottlieb, was formerly Manager of "The Pelican",
and was dismissed when it was found that his accounts
were not in order, and he had been making considerable
personal profits on the side.

As I understand it, Sir Victor Sassoon
gave no publicity in the matter owing to Gottlieb
being a refugee, so this is, to some extent, con-
fidential. Further enquiries are being made and
a report will be forwarded to you.

Yours sincerely,

Sd. K. M. Bourne.
Commissioner of Police.

Plan Formisl）

机密

尊敬的赫伯特爵士：

回复您1939年12月1日关于《字林西报》上一则广告的来函，此事已由特别处进行调查。广告发布者戈特利布曾是“鹈鹕”夜总会的经理，当发现其账目混乱且私下谋取巨额个人利润时，他被解雇了。

据我所知，维克多·沙逊爵士（Sir Victor Sassoon）因戈特利布是难民而未对此事公开宣扬，因此这在一定程度上是保密的。正在进行进一步调查，并将向您提交报告。

此致，

签名 K. M. Bourne.
警务处处长。

BRITISH CONSULATE-GENERAL,
SHANGHAI.

December 1st, 1939.

Dear Bourne,

I enclose a copy of an advertisement which
appeared in the North China Daily News on
November 23rd. At best it sounds suspicious
and at worst it savours of white slave traffic.
I understand from the Advertising Manager of
the North China Daily News that it was inserted
by one Gottlieb, who resides at the address
given, and that they were satisfied it was above
board. I had difficulty however in eliciting
the grounds for their satisfaction, and I should
be grateful if you could look into the matter
and let me know who this Gottlieb person is and
what is the real nature of his activities.

Yours sincerely,
〔此处转录不清〕

Major K.V. Bourne, M.C.,
Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.
pages.zh:
英国驻上海总领事馆，
上海。

1939年12月1日。

亲爱的伯恩：

随函附上11月23日刊登在《字林西报》上的一则广告副本。往好里说，这听起来可疑；往坏里说，这带有贩卖白奴的色彩。我从《字林西报》的广告部经理处获悉，该广告是由一名叫戈特利布的人刊登的，他居住在广告给出的地址，且报社确信此事光明正大。然而，我很难探明他们确信的根据，如果您能调查此事，并告知我这位戈特利布是何许人以及其活动的真实性质，我将不胜感激。

此致，
〔此处转录不清〕

K.V. Bourne 少校，M.C.,
警务处处长，
上海公共租界工部局，
上海。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section I, Special Branch.
REPORT
File No. D.9564(C)
Date December 4, 19 39.

Subject Arthur GOTTLIEB, ex-manager of Pelican Night Club, Cathay Hotel.

Made by D. S. Pitts. Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

I attach herewith a copy of a state-
ment signed by Arthur GOTTLIEB, Hungarian Jewish
refugee, the former manager of the Pelican Night
Club at the Cathay Hotel.

The statement, which is in the form of
a confession, is self-explanatory and was made in
the presence of Dr. O. Fischer, well known local
lawyer.

This confession was the result of
complaints made by numerous patrons of the Pelican
Night Club, especially in September and October
of this year of the excessive prices being charged.

On November 5, 1939 on instructions from
the D. C. (Special Branch), GOTTLIEB was interro-
gated by the undersigned in respect of these
charges and his room in the Cathay Hotel was
searched after he had been found trying to smuggle
cigarettes and liquor from the hotel premises.

The value of liquor and cigarettes
found in his room amounted to $1857.20.

The Cathay Hotel management, in the
shape of Sir Victor Sassoon, did not desire to
press home a charge in the event of GOTTLIEB
making a full confession. This was explained
to GOTTLIEB who, after he had discussed the matter
with his legal adviser, Dr. O. FISCHER, made the
attached statement in Fischer's office.

At no time was GOTTLIEB coerced into

主题：亚瑟·戈特利布（Arthur GOTTLIEB），前鹈鹕夜总会经理，华懋饭店。

制作人：D. S. Pitts。转呈人：D. I. Crawford。

兹附上由亚瑟·戈特利布签署的声明副本一份，他是匈牙利犹太难民，前华懋饭店鹈鹕夜总会经理。

该声明以认罪书的形式呈现，内容不言自明，是在当地知名律师 O. Fischer 博士在场的情况下作出的。

这份认罪书是由于众多鹈鹕夜总会顾客投诉的结果，特别是今年九月和十月，投诉收费过高。

1939年11月5日，根据特别处副主任（D. C. (Special Branch)）的指示，笔者就这些指控讯问了戈特利布，并在发现他试图从酒店区域走私香烟和酒酒后，搜查了他在华懋饭店的房间。

在他房间发现的酒水和香烟价值共计 $1857.20。

SHANGHAI, November 9, 1939.

Manager,
Cathay Hotel Ltd.
Shanghai.

Dear Sir:

Referring to my position as manager of the American
Night Club and to the unfortunate happenings there I wish to
make the following statement:

1) I admit that I have sur-charged bills of some of
the guests in my capacity as manager of the American Night Club.

2) When the sur-charge was made on cigars, cigarettes,
bottles of wine and champagne, I used to take a part of the same
to my room.

3) I also admit that I have surcharged some of the bills
of guests with drinks served by the glass, such as Whiskey-Soda,
Brandy-Soda, Liqueurs, etc. For these drinks I used to keep an
account with the Bar Boy and when the value of such drinks amounted
to a certain sum, to cover two or three bottles of Whiskey, etc.
I took out of the bar nearly as many bottles as would cover the
amount of the individual overcharged drinks.

4) That I have been doing this overcharging of bills
either with full bottles or with separate drinks since on or about
the 15th March 1939 and have continued at intervals so to do up to
the time of my dismissal.
pages.zh:
上海，1939年11月9日。

经理，
华懋饭店有限公司
上海。

尊敬的先生：

鉴于我担任美国夜总会经理的职位以及那里发生的不幸事件，我愿作如下声明：

1) 我承认，在我担任美国夜总会经理期间，我对部分客人的账单进行了超额收费。

2) 当对雪茄、香烟、瓶装葡萄酒和香槟进行超额收费时，我会将其中的一部分拿到我的房间。

3) 我还承认，我对部分客人按杯供应的饮料账单进行了超额收费，如威士忌苏打、白兰地苏打、利口酒等。对于这些饮料，我与酒吧侍者保持账目记录，当此类饮料的价值达到一定金额，足以抵两到三瓶威士忌等时，我就从酒吧取出相应数量的酒瓶，以抵消个别被超额收费的饮料金额。

4) 我自1939年3月15日左右开始，无论是整瓶还是单杯饮料，一直进行这种账单超额收费行为，并断断续续持续到我被解雇之时。

pages.en:
-2-

5) That the bottles thus removed by me to my room
No.620 Cathay Hotel, are those found there on Sunday, 5th
November, viz. 10 bottles Bollinger, 5 bottles Pommery e Greno,
Vintage, 1 bottle Pommery e Greno Sec, 3 bottles Veuve Clicquot,
2 bottles Berncasteler, to which have to be added the bottles found
in my possession when leaving the Hotel, about 12.30 p.m. on Sunday,
5th November 1939, viz. 2 bottles Martell's Brandy, 1 bottle Gordon
Gin, 50 Craven "A" Cigarettes (20's) and about 1 bottle of Red Wine,
6-7 bottles Liquors and Whiskey which I gave to third parties as
presents and 2-3 bottles of Liquors which were consumed in my room.
For all other drinks consumed in my room I have duly signed chits
for the same.

6) I swear and confirm that I have not sold neither
inside nor outside of the Hotel any of these goods but except
those found in my room and/or consumed there I have made presents
of the same to friends and/or refugees, not knowing whether such
persons were using them for their own consumption or for any other
purposes. It is for this very reason that I felt and was under
the impression that I was not stealing or doing anything illegal
in making these surcharges and removing the bottles to my room
and I therefore in no way whatsoever have been acting for the
purposes of personal profit or gain.

My sole intention and aim was to increase the takings
of the Pelican Night Club, not deriving thereby even an increase
in my share of commission as the turnover reached by me was much
more than twice than required.
pages.zh:
-2-

5) 因此被我移至华懋饭店620号房间的瓶子，即是11月5日星期日在那里发现的瓶子，即：10瓶 Bollinger 香槟，5瓶 Pommery e Greno 年份香槟，1瓶 Pommery e Greno Sec 干型香槟，3瓶 Veuve Clicquot 香槟，2瓶 Berncasteler 葡萄酒，此外还需加上我在1939年11月5日星期日下午12:30左右离开酒店时被发现持有的瓶子，即：2瓶 Martell 白兰地，1瓶 Gordon 金酒，50支 Craven "A" 香烟（20支装）和约1瓶红酒，6-7瓶我已作为礼物送给第三方的利口酒和威士忌，以及2-3瓶在我房间内消耗掉的利口酒。对于在我房间内消耗的所有其他饮料，我都 duly signed chits（正式签单）确认。

6) 我宣誓并确认，我未在酒店内外出售任何这些商品，除了在我房间内发现和/或在那里消耗的那些外，我将它们作为礼物送给了朋友和/或难民，我不知道这些人是将它们用于自己消费还是其他目的。正是出于这个原因，我觉得并认为我在进行这些超额收费并将瓶子移至我房间时，并没有偷窃或做任何非法的事情，因此我绝没有为了个人牟利或获益的目的行事。

我唯一的意图和目的是增加鹈鹕夜总会的收入，由此我甚至没有增加我的佣金份额，因为我实现的营业额超过了要求两倍之多。

pages.en:
-3-

7) I am now absolutely convinced that no one of the
management knew of my doings and I deeply and sincerely regret
the great and foolish mistake made by me and I beg for the
leniency of the Directors of the Cathay Hotel Ltd. for not
putting the case in Court owing to my situation as a refugee,
having my wife to support and also my mother and sister for
whom I have obtained a landing permit in Shanghai from the
Shanghai Municipal Council.

8, I furthermore and finally declare that I have no
claim of whatever kind or nature against the Cathay Hotel Ltd.

Yours faithfully,

(Signed by Mr.A.Gottlieb      (Sgd)   Arthur Gottlieb
in my presence                         _________________
"Dr. A. Fischer"
Barrister-at-Law.
Shanghai, 9th November 1939).
pages.zh:
-3-

7) 我现在绝对相信，管理层中没有人知道我的行为，我对我所犯下的巨大且愚蠢的错误深感真诚地后悔，并恳请华懋饭店有限公司的董事们宽恕，不要将此案诉诸法庭，考虑到我作为难民的处境，我需要供养妻子，以及我已从上海公共租界工部局为其获得上海登陆许可的母亲和妹妹。

8, 我此外并最终声明，我对华懋饭店有限公司没有任何性质或种类的索赔要求。

此致，

(由 A. Gottlieb 先生在我面前签署      (签名)   Arthur Gottlieb
"Dr. A. Fischer"
出庭律师。
上海，1939年11月9日)。

CONFIDENTIAL
DRAWER

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
British Consulate S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 9367 (c)
Shanghai. Date 29 12 39
December 29th 1939.

Dear Bourne,

Many thanks for your letter of December the
21st forwarding a copy of a report on the subject
of Gottlieb.

It would appear from this report that
Gottlieb is experienced in the training of
dancing troupes, and that there is accordingly
no reason to believe that he had any ulterior
motive in inserting the advertisement in question.
In these circumstances I propose to take no
further action in the matter.

With many thanks for your assistance,

Yours sincerely,
Herbert Phillips

Major K.M. Bourne, M.C.,
Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
SHANGHAI.

S/13-
Fee

1939年12月29日。

亲爱的伯恩：

非常感谢您12月21日的来信，并转来一份关于戈特利布事件的报告副本。

从这份报告来看，戈特利布在训练舞蹈团方面经验丰富，因此没有理由相信他在刊登相关广告时有任何不可告人的动机。在这种情况下，我打算不再对此事采取进一步行动。

非常感谢您的协助，

此致，
赫伯特·菲利普斯

K.M. Bourne 少校，M.C.,
警务处处长，
上海公共租界工部局，
上海。
